rule: Cedwyn editorial rule (25 Oct 2026): ingredients, not conclusions. Build-time rewording of conclusion sentences in mirrored theme text; cedwyn copy only, the datro sources are untouched. Each entry: theme, file (relative to the theme root), find (exact), replace, why. A find that is not present is reported, never fatal. — Sion's Tab agent

rewords.find: Our case, told forward: how Tŷ Mawr, the Great House of Llandough, an ancient Welsh home stewarded since 1667, became Church View Close.
rewords.replace: Told forward in dated steps: Tŷ Mawr, the Great House of Llandough, a home the family dates to 1667, and the land that is now Church View Close.
rewords.why: Stated the outcome as 'our case' in the page description; now states the start and end points and leaves the steps to the reader.

rewords.find: Our case: an ancient Welsh home, Tŷ Mawr, the Great House of Llandough, stewarded by one family since at least 1667, became Church View Close, an estate of twenty houses.
rewords.replace: The steps: Tŷ Mawr, the Great House of Llandough, a home the family dates to at least 1667, and the land where Church View Close, an estate of twenty houses, now stands.
rewords.why: Same conclusion in the About panel; reworded to the dated start and end points.

rewords.find: out comes A + B again as synthetic A3 and B, plus synthetic A1 and A2.
rewords.replace: out come the later titles, A3 and B, plus A1 and A2, which the family’s reading calls synthetic.
rewords.why: 'synthetic' was stated as fact in the description; now attributed to the family's reading.

rewords.find: Out comes A + B again, but as synthetic A3 and B, plus two more simple lines, SA1 and SA2, each born from a permissive occupancy ploy 💩.
rewords.replace: Out come the later titles, A3 and B, plus two more lines, SA1 and SA2. The family’s reading calls them synthetic and ties each to a step that treated the occupation as permissive; follow each line to its records.
rewords.why: 'synthetic' and 'permissive occupancy ploy' stated motive as fact; now attributed, with the reader sent to each line's records.

rewords.find:
1877 · Root title splits: Parcel A / Parcel B
TESTIMONY · later statement (c.1974)
rewords.replace:
1877 · Bute–Daniel Thomas arrangement and a Williams quarry lease, as later described by Mary (Nancy) Williams (c.1974). Parcel A and Parcel B here are provisional analytical polygons until the 1876–78 instruments and plans are overlaid
FAMILY TESTIMONY · later statement (c.1974) · grade 5
rewords.why: Parcel A/B is a working reconstruction resting on a c.1974 family statement; the 1877 instrument is not located [EV-0006].

rewords.find: It covered Parcel A: the last tenancy of Parcel A, whose occupiers the Williams family had been since 1667.
rewords.replace: How this “whole farm” letting maps onto the provisional Parcel A / Parcel B polygons awaits the tenancy and its plan (EV-0014). The family dates its occupation to 1667.
rewords.why: The judgment recites a tenancy of the “whole farm”; assigning it to one provisional parcel is our geometry, not the record. EV-0014 is known only through the 1987 judgment recital.

rewords.find:
1916 · Bute → John Williams (the son): yearly tenancy of the “whole farm”
VERIFIED · judgment
rewords.replace:
1916 · Bute → John Williams (the son): yearly tenancy of the “whole farm”
RECORD · judgment recital · grade 2
rewords.why: Label: the 1916 tenancy is a judgment recital (grade 2), not a document read.

rewords.find:
1928 · Last rent paid: Parcel A becomes the Williams family’s
TESTIMONY · Mary (Nancy) Williams
rewords.replace:
1928 · Last rent recalled by Mary (Nancy) Williams; she records that her father then “regarded the farm as his own”. The 1987 judgment records rent arrears in the mid-1930s and late 1940s, and a 1953 payment under a county-court judgment (EV-0080, EV-0030). No conveyance to the Williams family is identified
FAMILY TESTIMONY · grade 5 · set beside a judgment recital (grade 2)
rewords.why: Statement of belief, not a conveyance. Our own 1000 Cuts already sets the 1987 judgment beside it: arrears in the mid-1930s and late 1940s and a 1953 payment under a county-court judgment [EV-0080] [EV-0030].

rewords.find: its plan shows the eastern fields (Parcel B) only.
rewords.replace: its plan shows the eastern fields only (the provisional Parcel B). The plan fixes the extent of this 1939 letting; what WGR acquired in 1938 is a separate question that the 1938 conveyance and plan (EV-0019) would answer.
rewords.why: Tenancy extent and root-title extent kept separate.

1939 · WGR → John Williams agreement: plan shows Parcel B only

rewords.replace:

rewords.find:
1949 · First attempt to make occupancy permissive (the family’s case)
VERIFIED · judgment
rewords.replace:
1949 · John Williams’s tenancy surrendered after rent arrears; new yearly tenancy intended for Frederick Buckler, never put in writing
RECORD · judgment recital · grade 2
rewords.why: The judgment describes a surrender and re-grant after arrears; it is not an offer made to Mary and is not forced into a repeated-attempt template.

rewords.find:
4 Jul 1955 · Possession of Parcel B, later misread and conflated with Parcel A; the woodland and the green were also seized, shortly after Mary returned from hospital with her leg amputated
VERIFIED · judgment
rewords.replace:
4 Jul 1955 · High Court possession order enforced: “possession was taken in respect of all parts of the farm except the farmhouse and garden”
RECORD · judgment recital · grade 2
rewords.why: Judgment wording first; the woodland/green identification is labelled a working hypothesis.

RECORD · judgment recital · grade 2
rewords.why: Actor–action–object: an offer of a tenancy of the farmhouse and garden, refused (judgment); its tie to the green is the family reading.

29 Mar 1961 · Woodland: deed between Western Ground Rents, South Western Brick & Tile and Cardiff City Corporation, about 12 years after the 1949 attempt
VERIFIED · register read
rewords.replace:
29 Mar 1961 · Deed between Western Ground Rents, South Western Brick & Tile and Cardiff City Corporation, recited on the woodland register
RECORD · register recital · grade 2 (deed not read)
rewords.why: The 1961 deed is a register recital; its terms and plan are unread, so no interval pattern is attached to it.

rewords.find:
16 Jun 1970 · South-east ground registered as village green VG41 · about 11–12 yrs after the 1958/9 attempt
REPORTED
rewords.replace:
16 Jun 1970 · Village green VG41 registered by Glamorgan County Council
REPORTED · grade 3 · application, map and ownership section not yet read
rewords.why: A green registration rests on 20 years’ use as of right, not 12 years’ possession; on the certified VG41 map the green is a small roadside wedge [EV-0263]; our own interpretation layer already marks the 1970 reading as weakened (P-02).

rewords.find: An alteration to the Ordnance Survey’s “Ty-mawr” name for the farm in 1971; source pending until the 1971 OS sheet and its revision record are seen.
rewords.replace: On the Ordnance Survey 1:2500 sheet revised 1969 (published 1971) the name appears as “Ty Mawr Farm”, placed west of where earlier editions printed “Ty-mawr” (OS object name book, EV-0252). Why the name moved is an open question.
rewords.why: The audit treats the 1971 Ordnance Survey name change as source-pending. We hold the OS object name book (EV-0252) and the 1:2500 sheet revised 1969 (published 1971), which prints “Ty Mawr Farm” west of the earlier “Ty-mawr”. The reason for the move stays an open question.

rewords.find:
1974 · BP house: BP’s attempt to extinguish Mary (Nancy) Williams’s ownership claim fails
VERIFIED · pressCOURT PAPERS · not published here
rewords.replace:
1974 · BP Pension Trust’s county-court possession action adjourned part heard and never listed again; leave to enforce the 1962 order obtained, warrant later withdrawn; the licence letters follow (31 Oct)
RECORD · press (grade 4) + judgment recital (grade 2)
rewords.why: The 1974 county-court action was never heard and the warrant was withdrawn (EV-0049, judgment recital); but the Court of Appeal held the 31 Oct 1974 letters made her possession a licence. Both stated, no “fails”.
